examples.solution_text:
(a) The lowest common denominator is $15$. Multiply every term by $15$.
$\begin{align*}5x+3x&=120\\8x&=120\\x&=15\end{align*}$
(b) The lowest common denominator is $12$. Multiply every term by $12$.
$\begin{align*}3x-2x&=36\\x&=36\end{align*}$

The lowest common denominator is $12$. Keep each numerator grouped.
$\begin{align*}4(x+2)+3(x-1)&=60\\4x+8+3x-3&=60\\7x+5&=60\\7x&=55\\x&=\frac{55}{7}\end{align*}$

Multiply every term by $6$.
$3(x+3)-2(x-4)=42$
The minus sign applies to the whole second bracket.
$\begin{align*}3x+9-2x+8&=42\\x+17&=42\\x&=25\end{align*}$

Each side is a single fraction, so cross multiplication may be used.
$\begin{align*}6(x-3)&=4(x+1)\\6x-18&=4x+4\\2x&=22\\x&=11\end{align*}$

Multiply every term by $6$, including the whole-number term $2$.
$\begin{align*}2(2x+1)+12&=3(x-4)\\4x+2+12&=3x-12\\4x+14&=3x-12\\x&=-26\end{align*}$

(a) Multiply every term by $6$.
$\begin{align*}3x+2x-x&=60\\4x&=60\\x&=15\end{align*}$
(b) Multiply every term on both sides by $12$.
$\begin{align*}4(2x+1)-3(x-2)&=2(x+8)\\8x+4-3x+6&=2x+16\\5x+10&=2x+16\\3x&=6\\x&=2\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: (a) Multiplying by 15 gives 8x=120, hence x=15. (b) Multiplying by 12 gives 3x−2x=36, hence x=36.
Multiplying by 12 gives 4(x+2)+3(x−1)=60. Expanding gives 7x+5=60, hence x=55/7.
Multiplying by 6 gives 3(x+3)−2(x−4)=42. The subtracted bracket contributes −2x+8, giving x+17=42 and x=25.
Cross multiplication gives 6(x−3)=4(x+1), then 6x−18=4x+4, so 2x=22 and x=11.
Multiplying every term by 6 gives 2(2x+1)+12=3(x−4). Thus 4x+14=3x−12 and x=−26.
(a) Multiplying by 6 gives 3x+2x−x=60, so x=15. (b) Multiplying by 12 gives 4(2x+1)−3(x−2)=2(x+8), then 5x+10=2x+16, so x=2.
